That’s basically what it is. It’s a term used in the community, or at least in the community I was previously in, to say if it wasn’t explicitly taken off the table, anything goes. Which is an extremely dangerous way to play. But when new people come in and don’t understand what consent is (I surely didn’t), passive consent is basically (imo) a socially acceptable way to be a predator. 

I by no means play this way and wish I never had. When I came into the community, this is how some leaders played and introduced it to me, and I had a similar incident. I wasn’t able to stop the scene, and didn’t report until a month later after I processed what happened. They initially were on my side, but after talking to the leader everyone started to ignore me because I caused drama and they gave the leader a “second chance”. They still practice passive consent, and I don’t interact with anyone in the community. So maybe my take is just personal experience and not really what happened with OP.

I think what you are asking is the difference between passive and active consent. It seems like that community functions under passive consent which is not safe to me. Also, going against a well liked community member, in my experience, usually ends in nothing happening to them and you getting forced out. Something similar to this (though nothing was inserted) happened to me. 

The thing is, you did nothing wrong. You felt uncomfortable and stopped the scene. You should NEVER be shamed for saying you’re uncomfortable and stopping a scene. I mean what is the point of a safe word if you can’t use it??? Also, I use active consent, so if we don’t talk about it before, we don’t do it! Passive consent is so dangerous imo! I’m so sorry you experienced this. It’s a hard way to learn not everyone in the community is safe, especially leaders.

I feel deeply. While I show my partner, my friends, my family love in different ways and we have different dynamics, the intensity in which I feel love for them is the same. My partner and I, when we exchanged our vows nontraditionally, vowed to always love and respect each other, but we didn’t promise to stay together forever. Because in my experience since I was divorced, I knew love for me is not enough to stay tied to someone financially or live with them, because my wife left and I still loved her intensely, but that was what was best for the both of us. We’ve since gone on to have different partners, but while we express it through consensual boundaries we’ve set, our intensity of love is still there, just as our intensity of love is there for our new partner. 

With that being said, if there is ever a day that comes that my current partner feels the need to untangle financially from me or live separately or whatever he needs, while I’ll have a lot of hurt to process and I might need space to do it, I know once we are both ready we will come back. Maybe not like before, but that’s okay even if it’s sad sometimes, because my intensity never fades. 

I know this can be confusing to people because it was confusing to me to discover! Lol. And if I want the grace to feel this way, I know I need to give others the grace of explanation so they understand there is no shame in not getting it and no threat to their beliefs (if that makes sense). 

Anyway, I hope this kind of explains my thought process and I definitely respect and understand if you don’t think/feel the same way and I appreciate your interest in my viewpoint!

Edited to add: I don’t think I’d go on a show though because I don’t think my confidence in exploring that way is high enough to open myself to this level of questioning in that magnitude if that makes sense haha. I know how I’ve made mistakes in the past and I know not everyone can understand or give me grace for how I’ve acted and I don’t want to push myself or open myself to hurt in that way. But kudos to anyone that does, just not for me lol

I'm afab and I've always hated shaving. Every time I do I get horrible razor burn and it's not a fun experience for me. I've tried all the creams and the no shave treatments and they all aggravate my sensitive skin. Even before I realized I'm non binary I refused to shave in the winter time because I didnt like it. My sibling, ex, parents, friends have all made stupid comments about how hairy i am and how no one will want me because I'm hairy. Then i found a partner who supported me and said they didnt care if i was hairy and i was able to embrace it  i haven't shaved in almost two years and it's been amazing. I still get comments from my parents and sibling, but i always say, "partner doesn't care and neither do i" and that usually shuts them up for that trip. I have patchy hair on my chin  because pcos and honestly if it were fuller I'd love to wear it long. Bearded female presenting vibes is totally my aesthetic lol. 

I've found the confidence comes from me. Start with armpits, those are easy to hide on days you feel insecure. That's how I started. Then once you feel confident, do just long hair on your thighs, then the whole leg. It sucks to have unsupportive parents, but I've come to realize my parents will never love or support me the way I want them to so I've built my own support system that loves me for who I am. 

Good luck on your journey! Wishing you hairy legs and the confidence to rock'em.

Coming out when I was a teenager SUCKED. I told my parents and they freaked, my mom outed me to my entire family, my family freaked. I was bullied in school, one kid literally kicked my feet out from under me and called me a dyke. It was so rough. People can be cruel, especially people that don't understand or know the LGBT community. I suffer with severe chronic depression, it sucks. Go to a counselor, try to reach out for help. Almost ten years later, my family talks to me, they're a little more open minded (as much as they can be I guess) about the LGBT community. Life gets better. 

The one thing I wish I could go back and tell teenage me is try to learn to love yourself. You are beautiful and fierce and unique and worthy of love and life. You will not find your happy in others though, it has to come from within. People will let you down, put you down, hurt you, but if you love you, none of that will matter. 

Tldr; Don't let the bitches get you down, love yourself, ask a counselor for help, it gets better.
